body:
I'm wondering whether we need this warning at all. It seems super highly specific as seen in the condition that triggers it.

It's probably better to document clearly that those features only work when per pixel transparency is enabled and supported by the DisplayDriver, and remove the warning IMO.
The warning is for discoverability, so users don't have to go hunting the docs as to why their theme with shadows/round corners doesn't work.

This kind of warning for discoverability is a good idea in principle, but turns out to be problematic more often than not.

For example a user may be developing on a platform that doesn't support per-pixel transparency (and would raise that warning every single time they play the project, or in the editor as configuration warning if doing what @bruvzg suggests), but their target export platforms might support it just fine.

In such a scenario they'd be using the feature fine, but they would not be able to get rid of that warning on their dev environment.

Conversely, if they develop on a platform that supports it, but export to a platform that doesn't, the "discoverability" would come from being able to access logs (potentially of games in production) to find that they're relying on a feature that's not properly cross-platform.

We have a number of non cross-platform features and adding expensive checks for those in all nodes isn't really feasible IMO, calling it out in the documentation explicitly is the best we can do in my experience. We've tried approaches like this and it always leads to user frustration and bug reports that they want the warning to go away.
